sections.title: The sounds, and the accent that changes the word
bullets: Five vowels, one sound each, never reduced: a e i o u. English drifts its vowels, Spanish does not.
ñ is a letter, not a decoration: año is year, ano is not.
rr is trilled and meaningful: perro is a dog, pero is but.
h is silent, always. v and b are the same sound.
Castilian distinción: c before e or i, and z, are the th of think. cielo, zapato. Andalusia, the Canaries and all of America merge them with s, which is not an error, just not the model here.
Stress: a word ending in a vowel, n or s is stressed on the second-to-last syllable; anything else on the last. If the word breaks that rule, it wears a written accent.
Questions and exclamations open with ¿ and ¡. They are obligatory.

sections.title: Gender and agreement, the glue of the sentence
bullets: Every noun is masculine or feminine. -o is usually masculine, -a usually feminine, -ción, -dad and -tad always feminine.
Learn the exceptions with their article: el día, el problema, el mapa, la mano, el agua (feminine, but takes el in the singular).
Plural: add -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant, and -z becomes -ces. lápiz, lápices.
The article and every adjective must match the noun in gender and number. Adjectives in -e or a consonant do not change for gender.
The adjective goes after the noun by default. Before it, it becomes a judgement rather than a fact: un hombre grande is a big man, un gran hombre is a great one.
sections.diagram:

examples.target: Las ciudades españolas son muy bonitas.

sections.title: ser or estar, one decision
bullets: ser: what something IS. Identity, origin, profession, material, the time and the date.
estar: what state it is IN. Location, mood, condition, and the result of an action.
Some adjectives change meaning with the choice: es listo is clever, está listo is ready. es aburrido is boring, está aburrido is bored.
hay is the invariable there is or there are, and it never takes a definite article. hay un banco, never hay el banco.
New information takes hay; known information takes está. ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? against ¿Dónde está la farmacia?

examples.target: Es de Madrid, pero ahora está en Sevilla.
examples.gloss: He is from Madrid, but right now he is in Seville.

sections.title: The present, and the four irregular families
bullets: Regular: -o -as -a -amos -áis -an for -ar; -o -es -e -emos -éis -en for -er; -o -es -e -imos -ís -en for -ir.
e becomes ie: querer, empezar, pensar, entender, preferir.
o becomes ue: poder, volver, dormir, encontrar, costar. jugar does u to ue.
e becomes i: pedir, seguir, repetir, servir.
The nosotros and vosotros forms keep the plain stem in all three families. That is the boot shape.
The yo-form group is irregular in the first person only: hago, pongo, salgo, traigo, sé, veo, doy, conozco.

sections.title: Who you are talking to
bullets: Spain uses four second persons: tú and vosotros informally, usted and ustedes formally. This course teaches all four.
All of Latin America has lost vosotros and uses ustedes for every plural you, formal or not. You will hear that constantly and it is correct there.
Subject pronouns are normally left out, because the ending already says who. Put them in only for contrast: yo trabajo, tú no.
Parts of Latin America use vos instead of tú, with its own verb forms: vos sos, vos tenés. Recognise it, do not produce it here.
sections.diagram:

plural   vosotros     ustedes   (Spain)
plural   ustedes      ustedes   (Latin America)

sections.title: The object pronouns, and where they go
bullets: Direct: me te lo/la nos os los/las. Indirect: me te le nos os les.
Before a conjugated verb: lo veo. Attached to an infinitive, gerund or affirmative imperative: verlo, viéndolo, míralo.
With a periphrasis both positions are correct: lo tengo que hacer or tengo que hacerlo.
Indirect before direct, always. And le or les becomes se in front of lo, la, los, las: se lo doy, never le lo doy.
Spanish repeats the indirect object even when the noun is there: le doy el libro a Ana. English has no equivalent, so it feels redundant and is not.

examples.gloss: The report? I sent it to him yesterday.

sections.title: The three past tenses
bullets: he hablado, the pretérito perfecto: something inside a time period that reaches now. hoy, esta semana, este año, ya, todavía no, alguna vez, nunca.
hablé, the pretérito indefinido: something closed and finished. ayer, anoche, el año pasado, en 2019, hace dos años.
hablaba, the pretérito imperfecto: description, background, habit, age, weather, the time. No endpoint in view.
In a story the imperfecto paints the scene and the indefinido moves the plot: llovía cuando salí.
Most of Latin America uses the indefinido where Spain uses the perfecto, so hoy comí is normal there and hoy he comido is the peninsular form this course teaches.
sections.diagram:
hoy / esta semana / ya / nunca   -> he hablado

examples.target: Ayer fui al cine, pero hoy no he salido de casa.
examples.gloss: Yesterday I went to the cinema, but today I have not left the house.

sections.title: Orders, and the subjunctive hiding inside them
bullets: Affirmative tú: the third person of the present. habla, come, escribe. Eight irregulars: di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ven, sé, ve.
Affirmative vosotros: the infinitive with the final r turned into d. hablad, comed, escribid.
usted, ustedes and every negative order use the present subjunctive. hable, hablen, no hables, no habléis.
Pronouns attach to an affirmative order and come before a negative one: dímelo, but no me lo digas.
Attaching a pronoun often adds a written accent, because the stress has to stay where it was: compra becomes cómpralo.

sections.title: The present subjunctive: when, not why
bullets: Form it from the yo-form of the present, then swap the vowel: hablo becomes hable, como becomes coma.
Six real irregulars: sea, esté, vaya, dé, sepa, haya.
After wanting, asking, advising, forbidding: quiero que vengas, te pido que esperes.
After emotion and value judgements: me alegro de que estés aquí, es importante que estudies.
After doubt and denial, but not after certainty: no creo que sea against creo que es.
In clauses of purpose and of future time: para que lo uses, cuando llegues.
The other subject must be different. Same subject takes an infinitive: quiero ir, not quiero que yo vaya.

examples.gloss: When you have time, call me.
I do not think he is coming today.

sections.title: por or para
bullets: para: destination, purpose, deadline, recipient, opinion. Salgo para Madrid. Es para ti. Para mí, es fácil.
por: cause, exchange, duration, route, means, and on behalf of. Lo hago por ti. Pagué diez euros por el libro. Paso por tu casa.
The pair that shows the difference: trabajo para ella means she is my employer, trabajo por ella means I am covering her shift.

sections.title: The words that give you away
bullets: muy modifies adjectives and adverbs, mucho modifies verbs and nouns: muy cansado, trabajo mucho, mucha gente.
saber is knowing a fact or a skill, conocer is being acquainted with a person or place.
pedir is asking FOR something, preguntar is asking a question.
Spanish needs the double negative: no viene nadie, no hay nada.
gustar works backwards. The thing liked is the subject: me gusta el café, me gustan los libros. Same for encantar, doler, interesar, parecer and apetecer.
Write the accent. hablo and habló are different tenses and the exam grades the difference.

examples.target: A mis padres les encanta viajar, pero a mí no me gusta el avión.
examples.gloss: My parents love travelling, but I do not like flying.
